content.json:
# Keystone — Overview

_Read-only operational view of the Keystone Enterprise-Scale Landing Zone lab._

Queries source: **Azure Resource Graph** (cross-subscription, tenant-scoped to whatever the viewing identity has Reader on). Updates near-real-time (~minutes).

For live cost-by-resource / cost-by-MG analysis, use the **Cost Analysis** deep-links in the last section — Cost Management has its own UI and beats anything we could build here.

---

## Subscription inventory

Every subscription that lives anywhere under the `keystone` management group, including descendants. New Phase-2 subs (identity, workload-dev, workload-prod) appear here automatically as they vend.

content.query:
resourcecontainers
| where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
| where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
| extend MGPath = strcat_array(extract_all(@'"name":"([^"]+)"', tostring(properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain)), ' > ')
| project Subscription = name, State = tostring(properties.state), ManagementGroupPath = MGPath
| order by Subscription asc
content.title: Subscriptions under keystone MG

content.json:
## Resource inventory

Resources currently deployed across Keystone subs.

content.query:
resources
| join kind=inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
    | where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
    | project subscriptionId, SubName = name
  ) on subscriptionId
| summarize Resources = count() by Subscription = SubName
| order by Resources desc
content.title: Resource count by subscription

content.query:
resources
| join kind=inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
    | where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
    | project subscriptionId
  ) on subscriptionId
| summarize Count = count() by ResourceType = type
| order by Count desc
content.title: Resource count by type

content.query:
resources
| join kind=inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
    | where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
    | project subscriptionId, SubName = name
  ) on subscriptionId
| project Name = name, Type = type, Location = location, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, Subscription = SubName
| order by Subscription asc, ResourceGroup asc, Name asc
content.title: All resources under keystone MG

content.json:
## Policy compliance

Resources evaluated by the policies assigned at `keystone` MG scope. Non-compliant entries are the ones the platform team should be checking on.

content.query:
policyresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.policyinsights/policystates'
| join kind=inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
    | where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
    | project subscriptionId
  ) on subscriptionId
| summarize Resources = dcount(tostring(properties.resourceId)) by ComplianceState = tostring(properties.complianceState)
| order by Resources desc
content.title: Policy compliance state

content.json:
## Diagnostic-settings coverage

Which storage accounts under Keystone have a diagnostic setting forwarding to the platform LAW? The DfN policy at `keystone` MG scope should drive every SA to compliant — if any show `No`, the policy's managed identity or its role assignment is broken (CLAUDE.md §8 break/debug scenario).

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.storage/storageaccounts'
| join kind=inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions'
    | where properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain has 'keystone'
    | project subscriptionId, SubName = name
  ) on subscriptionId
| project SAId = tolower(id), SAName = name, Subscription = SubName
| join kind=leftouter (
    resources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.insights/diagnosticsettings'
    | extend ParentSAId = tolower(tostring(split(id, '/providers/microsoft.insights')[0]))
    | project DiagSettingId = id, ParentSAId
  ) on $left.SAId == $right.ParentSAId
| project StorageAccount = SAName, Subscription, HasDiagnosticSetting = iff(isnotempty(DiagSettingId), 'Yes', 'No')
| order by HasDiagnosticSetting asc, Subscription asc, StorageAccount asc
content.title: Diagnostic-settings coverage on storage accounts

## Cost views

Resource Graph KQL doesn't expose Cost Management data — those views live in the Cost Management UI. The links below open Cost Analysis pre-scoped to `keystone`:

- **[Cost by subscription (MTD)](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_CostManagement/Menu/~/costanalysis/scope/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Management%2FmanagementGroups%2Fkeystone)** — group by SubscriptionName.
- **[Cost by resource (high to low)](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_CostManagement/Menu/~/costanalysis/scope/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Management%2FmanagementGroups%2Fkeystone)** — same scope, then switch the group-by dropdown to *ResourceId* and sort by Cost desc.
- **[Cost by service](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_CostManagement/Menu/~/costanalysis/scope/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Management%2FmanagementGroups%2Fkeystone)** — same scope, group by ServiceName.

For CLI cost queries, see `scripts/cost-snapshot.sh` (uses the Cost Management REST API directly).

_A v2 of this workbook will embed cost-by-sub and cost-by-resource as native ARM-query cells. The ARM cell JSON is finicky and worth a separate iteration._
